 NVDA -6.62%

 Learn more Collecting $1,000 a month of passive dividend income from the Schwab U.S. Dividend Equity ETF (NYSEMKT: SCHD) takes a fairly large investment. But it's one that's certainly doable with the right plan. 
 Let's do the math, which starts with the total amount of income that needs to be generated: $1,000 a month translates to $12,000 a year. Right now, the Schwab U.S. Dividend Equity ETF pays an annualized yield of 3.1%. Based on this rate (which can change over time), investors would need to invest roughly $387,100 to hit that dividend income target.

 Image source: Getty Images. Based on the Nov. 17 closing price of $35.31, that means you would need to own approximately 10,963 shares of the fund to produce $1,000 of monthly passive income. 
 Obviously, most people probably don't have nearly $400,000 sitting around to do this. That just means you'll need to take the "brick-by-brick" approach. In other words, keep investing in the fund on a monthly basis until you hit that share count target. 
 For example, a $500 monthly investment in the Schwab U.S. Dividend Equity ETF, which has generated a 10% average annual rate of return, would grow to $387,000 in about 20 years. Double it to $1,000 per month, and you can hit the goal in under 15 years. 
 Whether investing monthly or in a lump sum, the Schwab U.S. Dividend Equity ETF and its portfolio of high-quality, high-yielding dividend stocks is one of the best ways to produce steady passive dividend income.
